---
title: "Factorized joint interactions"
---

The experimental native factorized-interaction component executes an explicit
conditional joint law over ordered participant occurrences. It provides a
shared-input packet route and an independently implemented direct CUDA route.
It is independent of Torch, Python, a model superclass, and a Cell lifecycle.
The [qualification record](../planning/interaction-layout-proposal-2026-11-02/VALIDATION.md)
separates host checks, actual device checks and measured performance.

## Operation and numerical types

For mechanism `m`, cell `c` and channel `d`, the operation is:

```text
gate[m,c] = sigmoid(bias[bias_id[m]]
                  + sum_k gamma[gamma_id[m,k]] * z[context[m,k],c])
y[target[m],d,c] += gate[m,c] * alpha[alpha_id[m],d]
                   * product_r x[participant[m,r],d,c]
```

Every forward overwrites the output, starting from zero. A mechanism has two,
three or four ordered input slots. Repeated slots and context terms preserve
multiplicity. Parameter-bank indices are independent of mechanism IDs, so
different mechanisms can share alpha rows, bias scalars or gamma scalars.
An empty context list produces `sigmoid(bias)`.

The layout distinguishes operation-local numerical occurrence ordinals from
canonical biological identity. It does not discover regulatory structure or
assign biological meaning. The [checked pattern adapter](../include/Cellerator/layout/factorized_interaction_pattern.hh)
binds an existing `ExplicitPattern` through an explicit ordered incidence map;
raw preparation instead accepts the caller's identity/epoch assertions.
This is one numerical law, distinct from the existing positive-part-squared
gated-product family.

| Numerical value | Axes |
| --- | --- |
| Participant values | `x[occurrence, channel, cell]` |
| Conditioning values | `z[context, cell]` |
| Per-channel coefficients | `alpha[parameter_row, channel]` |
| Gate scalars | `bias[bias_id]`, `gamma[gamma_id]` |
| Output | `y[target, channel, cell]` |

Activation storage, parameter storage and output storage explicitly select
FP16 or FP32; defaults are FP16. Products, gates and reductions use FP32.
Output cotangents and all five native VJP buffers are FP32. FP32 atomic
reductions may change summation order; the operation does not promise bitwise
reproducibility. There is no threshold pruning of sigmoid values, and product
derivatives remain valid when participant values are zero.

Long conditioning sums use compensated FP32 arithmetic, including multiplication
residuals. The per-invocation tape saves gates and stable sigmoid slopes, so a
gate rounded to one does not silently erase a small derivative. High-fan-in
problems use a shared compensated-reduction backend. The backend query reports
`packet`, `direct`, or `stable`; two requests using `stable` do not constitute a
comparison of the packet layout against direct execution.

The main numerical qualification domain uses finite `x`, `z`, `alpha` and
`gamma` in `[-1, 1]` and bias in `[-4, 4]`. The fixed corpus also declares
literal cancellation and sigmoid-saturation adversaries, including FP32 values
slightly above unit magnitude. Values outside the main domain are not clamped or scanned by
the low-level API; their accuracy requires separate qualification.

## Prepare topology and execute

[`factorized_interaction.hh`](../include/Cellerator/layout/factorized_interaction.hh)
defines the host records. Preparation groups compatible mechanisms into bounded
packets with distinct input/context dictionaries, local role references and
forward/reverse postings. It retains stable mechanism IDs and structure epochs.
Changing topology or the numerical binding of occurrences requires preparation
of a new compatible layout; changing values or parameters does not.

```cpp
#include <Cellerator/layout/factorized_interaction.hh>

namespace layout = cellerator::layout;
layout::FactorizedInteractionMechanism mechanism;
mechanism.logical_id = 1;
mechanism.arity = 3;
mechanism.inputs = {0, 1, 0, 0}; // Input 0 participates twice.
mechanism.target = 0;
mechanism.alpha = 0;
mechanism.bias = 0;
mechanism.terms = {{0, 0}, {1, 1}};

auto prepared = layout::prepare_factorized_interactions(
    {mechanism}, layout::FactorizedInteractionExtents{2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2});
```

[`modeling/cuda/factorized_interaction.hh`](../include/Cellerator/modeling/cuda/factorized_interaction.hh)
supplies the device owner, workspace query and asynchronous forward/VJP calls.
`FactorizedInteractionDeviceLayout` owns uploaded structural buffers; its
readiness and numerical-use lifetimes follow the declared stream contract.
It owns no numerical inputs, parameters or tapes.

Low-level calls allocate no memory and perform no synchronization. Callers
provide disjoint output, scratch and gradient buffers, and a per-invocation tape
for saved gates and slopes. They retain structure, immutable primals, parameters and tape
through backward and queued stream completion. Repeated VJPs need private
scratch/gradient destinations; a different stream requires an event dependency.
Opaque borrowed buffers do not acquire automatic mutation tracking or snapshots.
Structural descriptors and posting arrays must also remain disjoint from all
writable numerical buffers. Argument checks do not prove the provenance or
non-aliasing of every borrowed device allocation.

The [C++ training example](../examples/native_cuda/factorized_interaction_training.cu)
shows preparation, allocation, forward, all five VJPs and explicit parameter
updates. Allocation owners remain separate from model computation. The example
is buildable without a Torch dependency; running it requires admitted CUDA
execution.

## Optional Torch adaptation

The optional adapter exposes the same native law through ordinary Torch tensors
and first-order autograd. A prepared plan caches immutable structural uploads
per device; each invocation owns its tape and scratch. Numerical values and
parameters remain caller-owned tensors.

```python
import torch
from cellerator.torch import PreparedFactorizedInteraction

interaction = PreparedFactorizedInteraction(
    [{"logical_id": 1, "inputs": [0, 1, 0], "target": 0,
      "alpha": 0, "bias": 0, "terms": [(0, 0), (1, 1)]}],
    inputs=2, contexts=2, outputs=1, alpha_rows=1, biases=1, gammas=2,
)
x = torch.rand(2, 8, 32, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16,
               requires_grad=True)
z = torch.rand(2, 32, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16,
               requires_grad=True)
alpha = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.ones(1, 8, device="cuda"))
bias = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, device="cuda"))
gamma = torch.nn.Parameter(torch.ones(2, device="cuda"))
optimizer = torch.optim.SGD([alpha, bias, gamma], lr=1e-3)

optimizer.zero_grad()
y = interaction(x, z, alpha, bias, gamma, output_dtype=torch.float32)
y.square().mean().backward()
optimizer.step()
```

All tensors must satisfy the declared contiguous shapes and CUDA device/dtype
contract. Autograd returns each gradient in its input tensor's dtype; the native
VJP computes in FP32. Saved tensors use Torch's version checks. Higher-order
derivatives are rejected explicitly. The `route="direct"` option selects the
direct control request; high-fan-in workloads may select the shared stable
backend for either request. The host-layout C++ adapter is a convenience path
that prepares and uploads on each call; use a persistent prepared owner for
repeated execution.

## Build and evidence boundary

An installed native CUDA-enabled package exposes:

```cmake
find_package(Cellerator REQUIRED COMPONENTS factorized_interaction_cuda)
target_link_libraries(my_model PRIVATE Cellerator::factorized_interaction_cuda)
```

For a source build, follow the CUDA configuration in the
[developer reference](developer_reference.qmd) and enable
`CELLERATOR_BUILD_FACTORIZED_INTERACTION_EXAMPLE=ON`. The example target and
focused install component are:

```sh
cmake --build build --target cellerator_factorized_interaction_training
cmake --install build --prefix /path/to/prefix --component FactorizedInteractionCUDA
```

Packet preparation and host validation can be checked without executing CUDA.
CUDA compilation does not establish device correctness. The independent scalar
oracle and frozen workloads live in `tests/factorized_interactions` and
`bench/factorized_interactions`. Device validation, sanitizers and timing run
through the canonical Autobench/Scheduler route.

The packet representation is an experimental candidate. Reduced operand counts
are not measured memory traffic or a speedup. Preparation, upload, boundary
conversion, forward, backward, reductions and parameter refresh contribute to
the caller's complete cost. Use the qualification record for the exact cases
and supported performance conclusions; no biological validation follows.

The native delivery milestone is complete and independently reviewed.
Performance work is [paused](../planning/interaction-layout-proposal-2026-11-02/PAUSED.md)
with no accepted timing results. The current API defaults to the experimental
packet request; direct execution is explicit. No measured winner or production
route-selection policy has been integrated.
